mainTopic: The rescue of משה from the river (שמות 2:5-9): בת פרעה, her maidens, the astrologers' decree, משה's nursing, and מרים.
overview: This amud goes through the story of משה's rescue from the river (שמות 2), one phrase at a time. בת פרעה went down to the river to wash away her father's idol worship. Her maidens tried to stop her from saving משה, and גבריאל struck them down. רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argue whether אמתה means her maidservant or her arm. If it means her arm, it stretched out by a miracle. The גמרא explains why משה is called both ילד and נער, and how בת פרעה knew he was a Hebrew. Her word זה was a prophecy she did not understand: Pharaoh's astrologers misread a sign about water and canceled their decree once משה was put in the river. Two אמוראים give the date of that day, and a leap year makes both fit the three months of hiding. The amud ends with משה refusing Egyptian nurses, מרים and יוכבד, and the start of an explanation of why מרים is called 'the sister of אהרן.' That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that סוף means a marsh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the opinion that the סוף where משה's basket was placed was a marsh. It proves this from a פסוק that puts סוף next to reeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a marsh, as it says: 'The reeds and willows (סוף) shall wither.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation that began just before this section: the word סוף in the story of משה means a marsh. It brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו, סוף is listed together with קנה, reeds. Reeds grow in wet, marshy ground, so סוף must be a plant of the marsh. That means משה's basket was hidden among marsh plants.

keyTerms.meaning: A marsh or swampy pond full of reeds
As it is written; introduces a proof from a פסוק
A marsh plant, like rushes or willows

phrases.english: A marsh, as it is written:
"The reeds and willows shall wither."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 19:6

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲגַם, כְּדִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an opinion begun before this section, explaining the word סוף in ותשם בסוף.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that סוף means a marsh.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 19:6, where סוף appears together with reeds.

steps.title: בת פרעה went down to wash away idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, says בת פרעה's 'bathing' was spiritual. She was cleansing herself of her father's idols, and a פסוק in ישעיהו uses 'washing' the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe in the river.' רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: This teaches that she went down to cleanse herself from her father's idols. Similarly it says: 'When ה׳ will have washed away the filth of the daughters of ציון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק. It teaches that בת פרעה's bath was really a cleansing from idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רחץ, washing, can mean cleaning away sin and not just dirt. The proof is ישעיהו, where ה׳ 'washes' the filth of the daughters of ציון, meaning their sins. So בת פרעה's washing was a turning away from her father's idols.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches; introduces a lesson drawn from a פסוק
Idols (a disgusting term for idol worship)
And similarly it says; brings a parallel פסוק
Filth; here a picture of sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next steps. בת פרעה is shown as someone leaving her father's ways, which explains why she was willing to defy his decree and save משה.

phrases.english: "And the daughter of Pharaoh came down
phrases.notes: שמות 2:5

phrases.english: to bathe in the river,"
Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
This teaches that she went down to cleanse herself
from the idols of her father's [house],
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions just say 'her father's idols.'

phrases.english: And similarly it says:
"When ה׳ will have washed away
the filth of the daughters of Zion, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 4:4

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: מְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the meaning of סוף to the next phrase of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בת פרעה's bathing in the river was a spiritual cleansing from her father's idol worship.

steps.title: The maidens' 'walking' hints at their death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the word הולכות, 'walking,' used for בת פרעה's maidens, is a hint to their death. He proves it from עשו's words, 'I am going to die.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And her maidens walked.' רבי יוחנן said: This 'walking' is nothing other than an expression of death, as it says: 'Behold, I am going to die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the פסוק. רבי יוחנן says the maidens' 'walking' really means they were about to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה did not need to say that the maidens were walking, so רבי יוחנן reads the word as a hint. In בראשית, the same root הלך is used for going toward death. The step tells us the maidens died but not yet why; the next steps give the story.

phrases.english: "And her maidens walked, etc.,"
Rabbi Yochanan said:
This 'walking' is nothing
other than an expression of death,
and similarly it says:
"Behold, I am going to die."
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:32, where עשו says this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין הֲלִיכָה זוֹ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק, word by word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word הולכות hints that בת פרעה's maidens were going to their death.

steps.title: The maidens try to stop בת פרעה from saving משה
steps.stepSummary: When the maidens saw that בת פרעה wanted to save משה, they argued that a king's own household should be the first to keep his decree. They accused her of breaking her father's decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she saw the basket among the reeds.' Once the maidens saw that she wanted to save משה, they said to her: 'Our mistress, the way of the world is that when a human king makes a decree, even if the whole world does not keep it, his children and household do keep it. And you are breaking your father's decree?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story behind רבי יוחנן's hint about the maidens' death. This step gives their argument against saving משה and sets up the punishment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The maidens argue that if anyone keeps a king's decree, it should be his own family. פרעה had ordered that baby boys be thrown into the river, so his daughter of all people should not save one. This is the sin that leads to their death.

keyTerms.meaning: A human king (literally a king of flesh and blood)

phrases.english: "And she saw the basket among the reeds,"
Once they saw
that she wanted to save Moshe,
phrases.notes: Literally 'they want,' but the גמרא means בת פרעה wanted to save him.

phrases.english: they said to her: Our mistress,
the way of the world is
that when a human king makes a decree,
even if the entire world
does not keep it,
his children and household keep it,
and you are breaking your father's decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזוֹ דְּקָא בָעוּ לְאַצּוֹלֵי לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the background story that explains why the maidens deserved death, as hinted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The maidens tried to stop בת פרעה from saving משה, claiming she was breaking her father's decree.

steps.title: גבריאל strikes the maidens down
steps.stepSummary: The angel גבריאל came and struck the maidens to the ground. This is the death רבי יוחנן found hinted in the word הולכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גבריאל came and struck them to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: because the maidens tried to stop the rescue of משה, the angel גבריאל struck them down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes רבי יוחנן's teaching from step 3. The maidens' 'walking' meant going to their death, and here we see how they died. Once they were gone, nothing stood in the way of בת פרעה saving משה.
steps.whatToRemember: בת פרעה went to the river to cleanse herself of idol worship. Her maidens tried to stop her from saving משה, and גבריאל struck them down. This is why the פסוק hints at their death with the word הולכות.

phrases.english: Gabriel came
and struck them to the ground.
phrases.notes: This is the death רבי יוחנן found hinted in the word הולכות.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא גַּבְרִיאֵל וַחֲבָטָן בַּקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the maidens' protest in step 4 and completes רבי יוחנן's hint in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The maidens died at the hand of גבריאל for opposing the rescue of משה, which explains the תורה's hint that they were 'going' to their death.

steps.title: Arm or maidservant: the meaning of אמתה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argue over the word אמתה in the פסוק. One says it means her arm, and the other says it means her maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she sent her אמתה and took it.' One of רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה says it means her arm. The other says it means her maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק and brings an argument about what one word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אמתה can be read two ways. Read one way, it means a forearm, so בת פרעה reached out herself. Read the other way, it means a maidservant, so she sent someone to get the basket.

keyTerms.meaning: Her forearm or arm (from אַמָּה, a forearm or cubit)
Her maidservant (from אָמָה, a female servant)
One says... and one says: two opinions, without telling us who holds which

phrases.english: "And she sent her amatah and took it."
phrases.notes: שמות 2:5

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya disagree:
One says: her hand (arm),
and one says: her maidservant.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: יָדָהּ, וְחַד אָמַר: שִׁפְחָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the same פסוק, moving to its next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two readings of אמתה: her arm, or her maidservant.

steps.title: The reason behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: The 'arm' view rests on the word's meaning as a forearm. The 'maidservant' view says that if the פסוק meant a hand, it would have said 'her hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'her hand' learns it from the word אמתה, which means a forearm. The one who says 'maidservant' learns it from the fact that the פסוק did not simply write 'her hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side reads the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'arm' side takes the word at its plain meaning of forearm. The 'maidservant' side argues that the normal word for hand is ידה. Since the פסוק avoided that word, it must mean something else: a maidservant.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (introduces one side of an argument)
Since it is not written: a proof from what the פסוק leaves out

phrases.english: The one who says "her hand":
because it is written "amatah" (her forearm).
phrases.notes: Same letters, different vowels: אַמָּה is a forearm, and אָמָה is a maidservant.

phrases.english: And the one who says "her maidservant":
since it does not write "her hand."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר יָדָהּ דִּכְתִיב אַמָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind each side of the argument in step 6.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the פסוק: it uses אמתה instead of ידה

steps.title: Challenge to the maidservant view: weren't they all killed?
steps.stepSummary: If she sent a maidservant, how is that possible? We just learned that גבריאל struck the maidservants to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it was her maidservant, didn't you say that גבריאל came and struck them to the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'maidservant' view using what it said just before, in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the maidservants were killed because they objected to saving משה. If they were all dead, there was no maidservant left to send for the basket.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? This points to a contradiction with an earlier statement.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says "her maidservant,"
didn't you say:
Gabriel came and struck them to the ground!
phrases.notes: This is the death of the maidservants from just before, which רבי יוחנן found hinted in the word הולכות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שִׁפְחָתָהּ, הָא אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'maidservant' side by using the story from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that אמתה means her maidservant
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the maidservants were killed, so none was left to send.

steps.title: גבריאל left one maidservant
steps.stepSummary: גבריאל spared one maidservant, because it is not proper for a princess to stand alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left her one, because it is not the way of a king's daughter to stand by herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: not every maidservant was killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killing was real, but one maidservant was kept alive for the sake of the princess's dignity. That surviving maidservant is the one בת פרעה sent.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not the proper way

phrases.english: He left her one,
for it is not the way of a king's daughter
to stand alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּשַׁיַּיר לַהּ חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the earlier story: one maidservant survived.
steps.terutzMaskana: One maidservant was spared to accompany the princess, and she was the one sent.

steps.title: Challenge to the arm view: why not just say 'her hand'?
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק means her arm, why didn't it use the plain word ידה?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it was her hand, let the פסוק write 'her hand'!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns and challenges the other side, the 'arm' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same reasoning the 'maidservant' side used in step 7. If the תורה meant her hand, the normal word would be ידה, so why use an unusual word?

keyTerms.meaning: Let it write: it should have said

phrases.english: And according to the one who says "her hand,"
let it write "her hand"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר יָדָהּ, לִיכְתּוֹב יָדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 8, now challenging the opposite opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that אמתה means her arm
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק chose an unusual word when a common one was available.

steps.title: Her arm miraculously stretched
steps.stepSummary: The word אמתה, which also means a cubit, teaches that her arm stretched out a great length.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that her arm stretched out very far.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק used the special word: it is hinting at a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ידה would only tell us she used her hand. The word אמתה, which is linked to אמה (a cubit, a measure of length), tells us her arm grew long enough to reach the basket.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: This teaches us
that it stretched out a great deal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּאִישְׁתַּרְבַּב אִישְׁתַּרְבּוֹבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the unusual word as a hint to a miracle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The unusual word has no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: אמתה teaches that her arm miraculously stretched.

steps.title: Support: miraculous stretching elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: A known teaching says that בת פרעה's arm stretched. It compares this to the teeth of the wicked, which ריש לקיש reads as 'stretched' rather than 'broken.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: you also find this with the arm of בת פרעה, and with the teeth of the wicked. It is written 'You broke the teeth of the wicked,' and ריש לקיש said: don't read it as 'You broke,' but as 'You stretched out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the stretched-arm answer with an earlier teaching that already says so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted teaching lists בת פרעה's arm next to another case of miraculous stretching. ריש לקיש rereads a word in תהלים so that the wicked's teeth grew long instead of being broken. This shows that the idea of a miraculous stretching is already known.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't read it as... but as: rereading a word for a lesson

steps.whatToRemember: According to the 'arm' view, בת פרעה reached משה's basket through a miracle: her arm stretched out to it.

phrases.english: As the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא בְּאַמָּתָהּ שֶׁל בַּת פַּרְעֹה,
phrases.english: And similarly you find with the arm of Pharaoh's daughter,
and similarly you find with the teeth of the wicked,
as it is written: "You broke the teeth of the wicked,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 3:8

phrases.english: and Reish Lakish said:
Do not read "You broke,"
but rather "that You stretched out."
phrases.notes: The two words sound alike. He means the teeth grew long, the same kind of stretching as the arm.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: וְכֵן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא בְּאַמָּתָהּ שֶׁל בַּת פַּרְעֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 11 with an earlier teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That בת פרעה's arm miraculously stretched
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of 'the Master' together with ריש לקיש's reading of תהלים 3:8

steps.title: Why 'she saw him' and not just 'she saw'?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ותראהו, 'and she saw him,' adding an extra word ending. It should have just said ותרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she opened it and saw him, the child.' It should have said 'and she saw'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק and points out extra wording that needs explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says 'the child,' so the 'him' ending on the verb looks unnecessary. The גמרא asks what this extra ending is there to teach.

phrases.english: "And she opened it and saw him, the child."
phrases.notes: שמות 2:6

phrases.english: It should have said "and she saw"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתֵּרֶא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'him' ending is extra, since 'the child' is already stated.

steps.title: She saw the שכינה with him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that the extra 'him' teaches that בת פרעה saw the שכינה with the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: she saw the שכינה with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers what the extra word ending comes to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'him' refers to something she saw besides the child, who is already named. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says that something was the שכינה, resting with משה.
steps.whatToRemember: An extra word in a פסוק is often read as a hint: here, 'saw him' teaches that she saw the שכינה with משה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
That she saw the Divine Presence with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שֶׁרָאֲתָה שְׁכִינָה עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the extra word as a hint.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'him' ending is just extra wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that she saw the שכינה with משה.

steps.title: Why is the baby called both child and lad?
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק calls משה both ילד and נער, and those words do not seem to match.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And behold, a lad was crying.' It calls him a 'child,' and it also calls him a 'lad.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one פסוק uses two different words for baby משה. It is setting up the next step, which explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ילד is a young child, while a נער sounds older. Since the same פסוק uses both words for the same baby, the change in wording needs an explanation.

phrases.english: "And behold, a lad crying."
phrases.notes: שמות 2:6

phrases.english: It calls him "child,"
phrases.notes: Earlier in the same פסוק it says ותראהו את הילד, 'she saw him, the child.'

phrases.english: and it calls him "lad."

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי לֵיהּ יֶלֶד וְקָרֵי לֵיהּ נַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק (שמות 2:6) and moves on to its next word.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two different words ילד and נער in one פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same baby cannot plainly be both a young child and an older lad, so the second word seems unexplained.

steps.title: A child's body with a lad's voice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says משה was a child in age, but his cry sounded like an older lad.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: He was a child, but his voice was like a lad's. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the question. משה was a baby, but his crying voice sounded older.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer each word describes something different. ילד describes his age, and נער describes his voice. That is why the two words do not clash.

phrases.english: It was taught:
He is a child, and his voice is like a lad's,
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא יֶלֶד וְקוֹלוֹ כְּנַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the two words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two words between two different features: age and voice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two words seem to contradict each other about how old he was.
steps.terutzMaskana: ילד refers to his age and נער refers to his voice.

steps.title: That would give משה a defect
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה rejects רבי יהודה's answer, because a strange voice would be a flaw in משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him: If so, you have made משה רבינו into someone with a defect.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה pushes back. He says it cannot be that משה had an unusual voice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby with a deep, grown-up voice would have something abnormal about him. רבי נחמיה will not accept a reading that puts a flaw in משה, so רבי יהודה's answer is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone with a defect or blemish

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said to him:
If so,
you have made Moshe our teacher into someone with a defect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן עֲשִׂיתוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ בַּעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole of רבי יהודה's explanation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It attributes a physical defect to משה.

steps.title: His mother made him a little wedding canopy
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה explains that נער hints at a youth's canopy that יוכבד made for משה in the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches that his mother made him a youth's canopy in the basket. She said: Perhaps I will not merit to see his wedding canopy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה gives his own answer. The word נער hints that משה's mother set up a little wedding canopy for him in the basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, נער is not about his body or his voice. It points to the youth's canopy in the basket. His mother feared she would never see his real wedding, so she made one for him right then.

keyTerms.meaning: A youth's canopy, a small wedding canopy
The basket (ark) משה was placed in

phrases.english: Rather,
it teaches that his mother made for him
a youth's canopy in the basket,
phrases.notes: נעורים comes from the same root as נער. That is the link to the word in the פסוק.

phrases.english: She said: Perhaps I will not merit to see his wedding canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָשְׂתָה לוֹ אִמּוֹ חוּפַּת נְעוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the question in step 15, replacing the answer that was rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads נער as a hint to the youth's canopy, not as a description of משה himself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נער describes something about משה's body or voice.
steps.terutzMaskana: נער hints at the youth's wedding canopy his mother made for him in the basket.
steps.whatToRemember: ילד and נער are explained in two ways. רבי יהודה says child's body, lad's voice. רבי נחמיה rejects that, because it would give משה a defect, and says נער points to a youth's canopy in the basket.

steps.title: How did בת פרעה know he was Hebrew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the פסוק and asks how בת פרעה could tell the baby was Hebrew.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she had pity on him and said: This is one of the Hebrews' children.' How did she know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the end of the פסוק and asks a simple question. How could בת פרעה tell this baby was Hebrew? The next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has her say plainly that he is a Hebrew child, but nothing in it explains how she knew. The גמרא wants to know what sign she saw.

phrases.english: "And she had pity on him
and said: This is one of the Hebrews' children."
phrases.notes: שמות 2:6

phrases.english: How did she know?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא יָדְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next part of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sign showed בת פרעה that the baby was Hebrew

steps.title: She saw he was circumcised
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers that she saw the baby had a ברית מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Because she saw that he was circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is short. She saw the baby was circumcised, so she knew he was Hebrew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Circumcision was the clear sign of a Hebrew baby, and that is how she knew who he was.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
That she saw he was circumcised.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרָאֲתָה אוֹתוֹ מָהוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She saw that he was circumcised.

steps.title: בת פרעה prophesied without knowing it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the word זה hides a prophecy: this baby goes into the water, and no other baby will.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This.' רבי יוחנן said: It teaches that she prophesied without realizing it. This one falls, and no other falls.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן focuses on the single word זה, 'this.' He says בת פרעה was speaking a prophecy without knowing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, 'this' just points at the baby. רבי יוחנן reads it as 'this one is thrown into the water, and no other will be.' She meant something simple, but her words were saying more than she knew.

phrases.english: "This."
Rabbi Yochanan said:
It teaches that she prophesied without knowing it —
this one falls,
phrases.notes: 'Falls' here means being thrown into the river, like the Hebrew babies were.

phrases.english: and no other falls.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁנִּתְנַבְּאָה שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the last word of the פסוק quoted in step 19 and finds a hidden meaning in it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word זה is a hidden prophecy: this baby is thrown into the water, but no other baby will be.

steps.title: People can see the future without understanding it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר's reading of a פסוק in ישעיהו shows that people can glimpse or say something true without understanding it, which supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי אלעזר said: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'And when they say to you: Seek out the necromancers and the diviners who chirp and who mutter'? They see, but do not know what they see. They speak, but do not know what they are saying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's teaching to back up רבי יוחנן. It shows that someone can say true words about the future without understanding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads מצפצפים as related to צופין, 'they see.' He reads מהגים as 'they speak.' Those who look into the future do glimpse things, but they do not understand what they see or say. That is exactly what happened to בת פרעה when she said זה.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as

steps.whatToRemember: בת פרעה's word זה was a hidden prophecy she did not understand, just as רבי אלעזר teaches that people can see or say true things without knowing what they mean.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Elazar said,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And when they say to you,
Seek out the necromancers and the diviners
who chirp and who mutter":
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 8:19

phrases.english: They see, but do not know what they are seeing,
phrases.notes: צופין, 'see,' sounds like מצפצפים, 'chirp,' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: they speak, but do not know what they are saying.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's claim that someone can prophesy without knowing it.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching that בת פרעה prophesied without knowing it
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's reading of ישעיהו 8:19: they see and speak without understanding what they see and speak.

steps.title: The astrologers see a sign and decree that all baby boys be drowned
steps.stepSummary: פרעה's astrologers saw that ישראל's savior would be stricken through water, so they ordered every newborn boy thrown into the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: They saw that the savior of Israel would be stricken through water. So they decreed: 'Every son that is born, you shall throw into the river.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now applies the idea from step 22 to פרעה's astrologers. They saw a real sign, but they misunderstood it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The astrologers' vision was true: Israel's savior really would suffer because of water. They assumed it meant he would drown. So they tried to make that happen by throwing every baby boy into the river.

keyTerms.meaning: The savior of the Jewish people (משה)
Is stricken, punished, or suffers harm

phrases.english: They saw that the savior of Israel
phrases.notes: "They" means פרעה's astrologers. The גמרא names them in step 25.

phrases.english: would be stricken through water,
so they arose and decreed:
"Every son that is born
you shall throw into the river."
phrases.notes: שמות 1:22

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאוּ שֶׁמּוֹשִׁיעָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמַּיִם הוּא לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אלעזר's principle (seeing without understanding) to Pharaoh's astrologers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The drowning decree came from the astrologers' vision that Israel's savior would be stricken through water.

steps.title: The decree is canceled, but the astrologers misread the sign
steps.stepSummary: Once משה was put into the water, the sign disappeared and the decree was canceled. The astrologers did not realize the sign was really about מי מריבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once משה was put into the water, they said: 'We don't see that sign anymore.' So they canceled their decree. But they did not know that he would be stricken over the waters of מריבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: after משה was placed in the river, the sign stopped appearing, so the Egyptians canceled the decree. The גמרא then shows that they had misunderstood their vision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The astrologers thought putting משה in the water had fulfilled the sign. In truth, the 'water' was מי מריבה, where משה would later be punished. This is exactly the point of step 22: they saw something true but did not understand it.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'waters of strife,' where משה hit the rock

steps.whatToRemember: The astrologers' vision was true, but they read it wrong. משה's suffering through water happened at מי מריבה, not in the Nile.

phrases.english: Once they threw משה into the water,
they said: We no longer see
anything like that sign,
and they canceled their decree.
But they did not know
that he would be stricken over the waters of מריבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּשַׁדְיוּהּ לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the astrologers' story and reveals their mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The astrologers canceled the decree, not knowing that the water in their vision was really מי מריבה.

steps.title: A פסוק hints that מי מריבה is the water the astrologers saw
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא reads 'המה מי מריבה' as 'these are the waters the astrologers saw and got wrong.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: What does the פסוק mean, 'These are the waters of מריבה, where they strove'? These are the waters that פרעה's astrologers saw and got wrong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that supports the story it just told. A פסוק about מי מריבה hints back to the astrologers' mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word המה ('these') is read as pointing to something specific: these are the very waters in the astrologers' vision. This gives the story a basis in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what [so-and-so] said, used to bring a supporting teaching

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"These are the waters of Meribah, where they strove"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:13

phrases.english: These are the waters that Pharaoh's astrologers saw and got wrong.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק-based support for the claim that the astrologers' vision was about מי מריבה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the astrologers' vision referred to מי מריבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 20:13, 'המה מי מריבה', as read by רבי חמא ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: משה tells Israel they were all saved because of him
steps.stepSummary: משה's words 'שש מאות אלף רגלי' are read as 'you were all saved because of me,' since the decree was canceled on his account.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what משה meant when he said, 'Six hundred thousand on foot...' משה told Israel: Because of me, all of you were saved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another support for the story. משה himself hints that the decree was canceled because of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רגלי, which usually means 'on foot,' is read here as 'because of me.' Since the decree ended once משה was put into the water, every Jewish baby boy was saved thanks to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Usually 'on foot'; here read as 'because of me'
Because of me, on my account

steps.whatToRemember: The drowning decree was canceled because of משה, so all of Israel was saved through him.

phrases.english: And this is what משה said:
"Six hundred thousand on foot, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:21. Here רגלי is read as "because of me" instead of "on foot."

phrases.english: משה said to Israel:
Because of me, all of you were saved.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second support from a פסוק, showing that the decree was canceled because of משה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the decree was canceled because משה was put into the water.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 11:21, with רגלי read as 'because of me.'

steps.title: משה was put in the river on the twenty-first of ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא says the day was כ״א ניסן. The angels protested that the one who would sing at the Sea on that date should not suffer on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said: That day was the twenty-first of ניסן. The ministering angels said before הקב״ה: Master of the World, should the one who will someday sing the Song at the Sea on this day be made to suffer on this day?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי חנינא בר פפא tells us the date משה was put into the river, and what the angels said about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כ״א ניסן is the date the ים סוף would later split, when משה sang שירת הים. The angels argued that such a special day should not be a day of suffering for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The Song at the Sea (שירת הים)
Should he be stricken or suffer?

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said:
That day
phrases.notes: The day משה was put into the river.

phrases.english: was the twenty-first of Nisan.
The ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁעָתִיד לוֹמַר שִׁירָה עַל הַיָּם
phrases.english: the one who will someday sing the Song at the Sea
on this day, should he suffer on this day?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the decree story to the date משה was put into the river.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was put into the river on כ״א ניסן, the future date of the Song at the Sea.

steps.title: Another view: משה was put in the river on the sixth of סיון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא says the day was ו׳ סיון. The angels protested that the one who would receive the תורה on that date should not suffer on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר חנינא said: That day was the sixth of סיון. The ministering angels said before הקב״ה: Master of the World, should the one who will someday receive the תורה at הר סיני on this day be made to suffer on this day?
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא disagrees about the date. He says it was ו׳ סיון, and the angels make the same kind of protest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the angels protested because the date was special. They differ only on which future event made it special: שירת הים on כ״א ניסן, or מתן תורה on ו׳ סיון.

keyTerms.meaning: The sixth of סיון, the day the תורה was given

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new event. It is the same day (when משה was put in the river), and the two אמוראים simply disagree about which date it was.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said:
That day
was the sixth of Sivan.
The ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁעָתִיד לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה מֵהַר סִינַי
phrases.english: the one who will someday receive the Torah from Mount Sinai
on this day, should he suffer on this day?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שִׁשָּׁה בְּסִיוָן הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different date for the same event that step 27 dated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was put into the river on ו׳ סיון, the future date of מתן תורה.

steps.title: Does the twenty-first of Nisan fit the three months of hiding?
steps.stepSummary: The three months of hiding fit the opinion of ו׳ סיון, since משה was born on ז׳ אדר. The גמרא asks how three months fit the opinion of כ״א ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says it was on the sixth of סיון, you can find three months. The Master taught that משה died on the seventh of אדר and was born on the seventh of אדר. From the seventh of אדר until the sixth of סיון is three months. But according to the one who says it was on the twenty-first of ניסן, how can you find three months?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the two opinions from the last steps against the פסוק that משה's mother hid him for three months. One opinion fits easily, and the other seems too short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was born on ז׳ אדר. Counting to ו׳ סיון gives exactly three months, so רבי אחא בר חנינא's date works. Counting to כ״א ניסן seems to give only about a month and a half, which challenges רבי חנינא בר פפא's date.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works out fine (it opens a contrast with a view that has a problem)
You can find it / it can work out

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says it was on the sixth of Sivan,
you can find three months.
phrases.notes: This is the three months his mother hid him, from שמות 2:2.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
On the seventh of Adar he died,
and on the seventh of Adar Moshe was born,
and from the seventh of Adar until the sixth of Sivan
is three months.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן,
phrases.english: But according to the one who says it was on the twenty-first of Nisan,
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּשִׁשָּׁה בְּסִיוָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two dates from steps 27 and 28 against the three months of hiding.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בר פפא's view that משה was put in the water on כ״א ניסן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From ז׳ אדר to כ״א ניסן is less than three months, but the פסוק says he was hidden for three months.

steps.title: It was a leap year
steps.stepSummary: That year had two months of אדר. Part of the first month, all of the middle month, and part of the last month add up to three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: That year was a leap year. He was hidden for most of the first month, most of the last month, and the whole middle month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because that year had an extra month, the date כ״א ניסן also covers three months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two months of אדר, the hiding covers most of the first אדר, from the seventh day, then all of the second אדר, then most of ניסן, up to the twenty-first. Parts of the first and last months still count as months, so this is called three months.

keyTerms.meaning: A leap year, which has an extra month of אדר

steps.whatToRemember: Both dates for when משה was put into the water fit the three months of hiding. ו׳ סיון fits simply, and כ״א ניסן fits because that year had an extra אדר.

phrases.english: That year was a leap year:
most of the first,
phrases.notes: The first is the first אדר, counted from the seventh, when he was born.

phrases.english: and most of the last,
phrases.notes: The last is ניסן, up to the twenty-first.

phrases.english: and the middle one complete.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a fact about the calendar: that year had an extra month
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From ז׳ אדר to כ״א ניסן is only about a month and a half.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because there was an extra אדר, the hiding covered parts of three months, which counts as three months.

steps.title: Why did the nurse have to be Hebrew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where משה's sister offers בת פרעה a Hebrew nurse, and asks why a Hebrew woman specifically.
steps.simpleTranslation: His sister said to בת פרעה: 'Shall I go and call for you a nursing woman from the Hebrew women?' What is special about the Hebrew women?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next פסוק in the story and sets up a question. Why would the sister specifically offer a Hebrew nurse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בת פרעה was an Egyptian princess, so an Egyptian nurse would seem more natural. The פסוק's stress on 'Hebrew women' suggests there was a reason, and the גמרא wants to know what it was.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this one specifically?

phrases.english: "And his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter:
phrases.notes: שמות 2:7

phrases.english: Shall I go and call for you
a nursing woman from the Hebrew women?"
And what is different about Hebrew women?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מֵעִבְרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the date discussion to the next פסוק in the story of משה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק says the nurse had to be one of the Hebrew women

steps.title: משה refused to nurse from Egyptian women
steps.stepSummary: They first took משה to every Egyptian nurse, and he would not nurse. A mouth that would one day speak with the שכינה should not nurse something impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that they took משה around to all the Egyptian women, and he would not nurse. He said: Should a mouth that will one day speak with the שכינה nurse something impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The Egyptian nurses had already been tried and failed, so a Hebrew nurse was the only option left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sister's offer makes sense only if Egyptian nurses had already been tried. The reason given is משה's future: his mouth would speak with the שכינה, so it had to stay pure, even when he was a baby.

phrases.english: This teaches that they took Moshe around
to all the Egyptian women, every one of them,
and he did not nurse,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: פֶּה שֶׁעָתִיד לְדַבֵּר עִם הַשְּׁכִינָה
phrases.english: he said: A mouth that is destined to speak with the Divine Presence
should nurse something impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶחְזִירוּהוּ לְמֹשֶׁה עַל כׇּל הַמִּצְרִיּוֹת כּוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה had already refused every Egyptian nurse, because a mouth destined to speak with the שכינה should not nurse something impure.

steps.title: Support from a פסוק in ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in ישעיהו asks to whom knowledge will be taught. It answers: to those weaned from milk. The גמרא reads this as pointing to משה, who refused impure milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is written: 'Whom shall one teach knowledge?' To whom shall He teach knowledge, and to whom shall He make the message understood? 'To those weaned from milk, to those removed from the breasts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support what it just said about משה refusing to nurse. The one who stayed away from impure milk is the one chosen to receive God's knowledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links receiving God's teaching with being 'weaned from milk.' The גמרא reads this as a hint to משה, who kept away from the milk of Egyptian women. That is why he was fit to receive and teach the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written (bringing a פסוק as support)

steps.whatToRemember: The sister offered a Hebrew nurse because משה had already refused every Egyptian one. His mouth, which would speak with the שכינה, had to stay pure, as the פסוק in ישעיהו hints.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"Whom shall one teach knowledge, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 28:9

phrases.english: To whom shall He teach knowledge
and to whom shall He make the message understood?
"To those weaned from milk,
to those removed from the breasts."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support the answer in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that משה refused impure milk because he was destined to receive God's word
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 28:9, which says knowledge is taught to those weaned from milk

steps.title: מרים went quickly like a young woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the פסוק calls מרים an עלמה because she went with the quick energy of a young woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: Go,' and the young girl went. רבי אלעזר says: this teaches that she went quickly, like a grown young woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק in the story and explains the word עלמה used for מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרים was still a young child, yet the פסוק calls her an עלמה, a young woman. רבי אלעזר learns from this that she moved with the speed and strength of an older girl. She was eager to bring her mother quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This teaches' – introduces a lesson drawn from a פסוק

phrases.english: "And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: Go, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 2:8. The rest of the פסוק says 'and the young girl (העלמה) went', and that is the word being explained.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
This teaches that she went quickly, like a young woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָלְכָה בִּזְרִיזוּת כְּעַלְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the story past the offer of a Hebrew nurse (steps 31-33) to the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word עלמה shows that מרים went quickly and eagerly, like a young woman.

steps.title: מרים hid her words
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads עלמה as coming from the word for hiding: מרים kept her words hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says: 'the young girl' (העלמה) means that she hid (העלימה) her words.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different explanation of the same word עלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר read עלמה as 'young woman.' רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads it as coming from להעלים, 'to hide.' On his reading, the word tells us that מרים kept quiet and did not reveal what she was really doing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
"The young girl" means that she hid her words.
phrases.notes: He hears עלמה as sounding like העלים, the word for hiding something.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: הָעַלְמָה שֶׁהֶעֱלִימָה אֶת דְּבָרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different reading of the same word that רבי אלעזר explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עלמה comes from 'hiding': מרים concealed her words.

steps.title: בת פרעה prophesied without knowing it
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא hears הילכי as 'this is yours,' so בת פרעה unknowingly told יוכבד the baby was hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: Take this child away (הילכי).' רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says: she was prophesying and did not know what she was prophesying. הילכי sounds like 'here is what is yours.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next פסוק and finds a hidden meaning in בת פרעה's words to יוכבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple meaning of הילכי is 'take away.' But it sounds like הא שליכי, 'this is yours.' Without realizing it, בת פרעה spoke the truth: the baby really was יוכבד's own child.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Take away' – the word in the פסוק

phrases.aramaic: ״וַתֹּאמֶר לָהּ בַּת פַּרְעֹה הֵילִיכִי אֶת הַיֶּלֶד הַזֶּה״.
phrases.english: "And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: Take this child away."
phrases.notes: שמות 2:9

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
She was prophesying and did not know what she was prophesying:
"Heilichi" means: here is what is yours.
phrases.notes: He splits the word into two: הא, 'here,' and שליכי, 'yours.' The baby really was יוכבד's own son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מִתְנַבְּאָה וְאֵינָהּ יוֹדַעַת מָה מִתְנַבְּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הילכי hints at הא שליכי: בת פרעה unknowingly prophesied that the child was יוכבד's.

steps.title: צדיקים get back what they lost and are paid too
steps.stepSummary: From 'and I will give you your wages,' רבי חמא ברבי חנינא learns that צדיקים get their lost item back and are also paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק continues: 'And I will give you your wages.' רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says: it is not enough for the righteous that their lost item is returned to them. They are also given their wages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the rest of the same פסוק and draws a lesson about how ה׳ treats צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוכבד got her own baby back, which is her 'lost item.' On top of that, she was paid for nursing him. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא turns this into a general rule: צדיקים get back what they lost and receive extra reward besides.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not enough for them

steps.whatToRemember: יוכבד got her son back AND was paid to nurse him. This shows that צדיקים get back what they lost and get reward on top of it.

phrases.english: "And I will give you your wages."
Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
It is not enough for the righteous
that their lost item is returned to them,
phrases.notes: The 'lost item' here is the baby משה, who comes back to his mother.

phrases.english: rather, they are also given their wages.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא דַּיָּין לַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁמַּחְזִירִין לָהֶן אֲבֵידָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same speaker, same פסוק: now explains its second half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים get back what they lost and receive their reward as well.

steps.title: Why is מרים called the sister of אהרן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a later פסוק calling מרים 'the sister of אהרן' and asks why it does not say 'the sister of משה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And מרים the prophetess, the sister of אהרן, took...' Why does it say the sister of אהרן and not the sister of משה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא jumps to a פסוק in שירת הים and asks about how מרים is described. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה is the main figure, and מרים watched over him at the river. So we would expect the פסוק to call her his sister. The גמרא wants to know what the unusual wording is coming to teach.

phrases.english: "And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 15:20

phrases.english: The sister of Aaron, and not the sister of Moses?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחוֹת אַהֲרֹן וְלֹא אֲחוֹת מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a different פסוק about מרים, opening a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק calls מרים the sister of אהרן rather than the sister of משה.

steps.title: מרים prophesied before משה was born
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב, the גמרא answers that מרים was already prophesying when she was only אהרן's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said in the name of רב, and some say רב נחמן said in the name of רב: this teaches that she was prophesying when she was still only the sister of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling her 'sister of אהרן' points to a time when אהרן was her only brother, before משה was born. That tells us her prophecy started back then. The גמרא is about to tell us what she prophesied.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Sister of אהרן' does not mean she was not משה's sister. It points to the time before משה was born, when she already had נבואה.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and some say it: Rav Nachman said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיְתָה מִתְנַבְּאָה כְּשֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אַהֲרֹן,
phrases.english: This teaches that she was prophesying when she was the sister of Aaron,
phrases.notes: That is, before משה was born, when אהרן was her only brother. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיְתָה מִתְנַבְּאָה כְּשֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording shows that מרים already had נבואה before משה was born, when she was only אהרן's sister.
